newsitem.title: MEXICO: Murdered Mexican foresees death in postmortem letter.
newsitem.headline: Murdered Mexican foresees death in postmortem letter.

text.p: A murdered former Mexican beauty queen predicted her own death days before she was gunned down mafia-style last week, Mexico's top law enforcement agency said late on Tuesday.
Irma Ibarra, 44, was shot at least six times when stopped at a red light in the western city of Guadalajara last week, in a suspected payback from drug traffickers.

In a notarized letter to her family dated May 9, she said powerful drug lords were plotting "a car accident" because she reported their activities to the government, Mexico's Attorney General's Office (PGR) said in a statement.

"I want to leave a testimony that if anything happens to me without a motive, I blame Eduardo Gonzalez Quirarte because I have received persistent threats," the letter, reprinted in the statement, read.
She said Gonzalez and Ricardo Jimenez, whom she also accused of threatening her, were drug traffickers who collaborated with Mexico's former drug czar Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo.
Gutierrez Rebollo, the former head of the National Institute for Combating Drugs, was arrested in February and charged with taking payoffs from druglords.

"(These threats) have happened because I found out the illicit acitivities of Eduardo Gonzalez and I dared them to comment to Gen. Gutierrez Rebollo, who I esteemed without knowing he was friends with these guys," the letter read.
Ibarra was suspected of being a social coordinator between military and drug lords. Her killers have not yet been found.
Her killing occurred during a recent surge of drug-related crime in Mexico, as drug lords settle scores and battle for turf in the wake of the death of Mexico's most wanted drug trafficker.
Amado Carrillo Fuentes' death on July 4 set off sparring between competing drug lords in key drug trafficking territory Guadalajara and Cuidad Juarez.
Six people were murdered in Ciudad Juarez on Monday in an armed attack on a restaurant, in a crime suspected to be part of the drug lord turf wars.
